items.title: Bobby Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: Casper Reardon and a couple of others came along.

ctx.x: Where do you feel you fit in to the sound of your fellow clarinetists. Do you emulate anybody? Were you highly influenced by anybody besides Joe Marsala?

I was highly influenced by Pee Wee Russell quite a bit. I always enjoyed his playing. And the type of playing that I really like to do myself is I used to work with Joe Marsala’s wife, Adele Girard. She was a great jazz harpist. She was the first swing harpist to come along in the 1900s. Casper Reardon and a couple of others came along. But I used to just like to play with her and Joe and play together, two clarinets and jazz
harp, which is very nice, it has a very pretty sound. And that was probably some of the most fun I’ve ever had playing.
